prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1488; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a left-turn collision at an intersection, with the claimant's vehicle struck on the driver's side. Initial file review started and a photo request went out to the insured.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the loss. No issues with policy status found.

Entry 3: Police report received. It places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and matches the general description the insured gave.

Entry 4: Photos from the insured and the claimant's side show the damage concentrated where the impact would be expected, and the overall pattern fits the described collision.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. Most of the damage lines up with the reported impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the appraiser's notes.

Entry 6: Claimant is represented by counsel. All communication now routes through the attorney's office, and a letter of representation is on file.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical summary from the first treatment visit. The neck and back strain described is consistent with the force of this type of crash, and no earlier injury to the same area is known from prior records.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course of care, with visits becoming less frequent as the claimant's symptoms eased. Notes indicate steady improvement over the period.

Entry 9: No independent witnesses have come forward. The photos confirm several details of the collision, but the account rests mainly on the parties and the police report.

Entry 10: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each contact so far, including the recorded statement, the attorney's letter, and the follow-up call.

Entry 11: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date. Coverage timeline checked against the vehicle's loss history and found clear.

Entry 12: File is in order for the next stage of evaluation. Bodily injury and property damage reserves reviewed, and the claim remains open pending the attorney's demand package.
